title: Fix the Unsafe Realloc Pattern
description: The program should grow a dynamically allocated array using realloc.
expectedBehavior: The array should be safely resized to hold 10 ints, and the program should print 42.
actualProblem: Assigning realloc's result directly back into arr means that if realloc happens to fail and returns NULL, the only pointer to the original 5-int block is immediately overwritten and lost — a memory leak — before the NULL check even runs.
explanation: realloc() should be assigned to a separate temporary pointer first. If it returns NULL, the original block is still valid (and can be freed); only once success is confirmed should the original pointer variable be updated to the new block.
